target.title: fix(qqbot): limit channel API targets to configured groups [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQBot channel API tool calls could request QQ guild or channel resources without applying the operator-configured QQBot group scope.

## Why This Change Was Made

The QQBot channel API executor now receives the active OpenClaw config and account id from tool registration, classifies guild/channel targets from the requested API path, and checks those targets with the existing QQBot group policy resolver before making the outbound QQ API request. Scoped configurations deny broad guild listing and out-of-scope guild/channel paths before fetch; wildcard group scope and unscoped configurations keep the existing behavior.

AI-assisted: yes.

## User Impact

Operators who configure QQBot group scope get the same target boundary on the raw QQ channel API tool. Existing unscoped or wildcard-scoped setups continue to use the channel API proxy normally.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check`
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write --threads=1 extensions/qqbot/src/engine/tools/channel-api.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/tools/channel-api.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/tools/channel.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/tools/channel-api.test.ts` (14 tests passed)

Proof gap: remote Testbox/Crabbox validation was not available in this workspace because the Crabbox and Blacksmith CLIs were not installed; the focused local fallback above passed.


- Runtime proof (credentialless, no secrets): direct executor probe with a redacted invalid token returned local scoped denial for `groups: { G1: {} }` on `/users/@me/guilds`; wildcard and unscoped probes reached the QQ endpoint and returned upstream `token not exist or expire` with status 500.
